analysis_scope.sampling_notes: The analysis context describes a shallow clone with depth 50, so history should be treated as recently sampled even though `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` returned false. All four locally available commits, all 32 tracked files, all notebook source cells, representative recorded outputs, the architecture PDF, and all ten tuner trial records were inspected; binary HDF5 weight contents were not decoded.

observed_capabilities.statement: The notebooks organize TIFF microscopy images into eight red-blood-cell morphology classes using filename patterns.

The repository implements TensorFlow/Keras Vision Transformer classifiers with patch extraction, positional embeddings, multi-head attention, dense classifier heads, augmentation, class weighting, and random-search hyperparameter tuning.
Recorded runs loaded 649 images across eight classes, split into 523 training and 126 validation images.
One notebook records a tuned model reaching 59.52% validation accuracy, while the later final notebook records 46% classification accuracy and predictions confined to the majority echinocyte class.

planned_work.statement: The architecture draft suggests a future Streamlit interface for uploaded-image classification and image generation, but no corresponding application implementation is tracked.

architecture.statement: Data preparation is notebook-driven: files are selected by morphology names embedded in TIFF filenames and copied into class directories consumed by Keras directory generators.
The classifier converts 64-by-64 RGB images into patches, adds positional embeddings, processes them with transformer encoder blocks, and applies a dense softmax head for eight-class prediction.
Experiment state is stored as Keras Tuner JSON records and three HDF5 weight checkpoints under `my_dir/hparam_tuning`.

accomplishments.statement: The repository demonstrates an end-to-end experimental workflow from filename-based dataset organization through model construction, training, tuning, validation, and classification reporting.
Executed notebooks preserve evidence of ten-trial and eighty-trial hyperparameter searches, model summaries, training histories, class distributions, and evaluation results.
The final experiment explicitly measures class imbalance and applies balanced class weights during tuning.

gaps.statement: The repository has no documentation explaining its purpose, data provenance, setup, execution order, expected results, or model limitations.
The source dataset is absent and several notebooks depend on hard-coded absolute paths to an external drive or a specific user directory, preventing reproduction from the checkout alone.
There are no pinned dependencies, tests, CI workflows, reusable Python modules, or deployable inference application.
Two tracked notebooks are empty, and the final notebook saves a `.keras` model that is not present in the tracked tree.

risks.statement: The final classification report is not reliable evidence of per-class performance because the validation generator is shuffled while predictions are compared with labels in their original stored order.
The final recorded model effectively predicts only the majority echinocyte class, producing zero precision and recall for seven classes despite 46% aggregate accuracy.
Validation images receive stochastic augmentation from the same generator configuration as training images, which makes evaluation variable and less representative of a fixed holdout set.
The final tuner declares `num_layers` and `dropout_rate` hyperparameters that are not actually used by the model-building call, so the reported optimum overstates what was tuned.
Recorded performance is internally inconsistent: the `image_vit` notebook reports a best validation accuracy of 59.52%, while every committed tuner trial record reports 46.03%.
Approximately 88 MB of generated HDF5 checkpoints are committed without visible Git LFS or generated-artifact controls, increasing repository size and obscuring which checkpoint is authoritative.

suggested_next_actions.statement: Document the coursework objective, dataset provenance and access requirements, environment setup, notebook execution order, and the limitations of the recorded results.
Refactor shared preparation and model code into reusable modules, replace machine-specific paths with configuration, and pin a reproducible environment.
Re-run evaluation with an unaugmented, non-shuffled validation generator and report a confusion matrix plus macro-averaged metrics before treating the model as a meaningful classifier.
Either implement and document the proposed Streamlit inference flow or remove the architecture draft so the repository does not imply a deployable application that is absent.
Choose one authoritative model artifact, record how it was produced, and move disposable tuning checkpoints out of normal Git tracking.

questions: Was this repository solely a completed Advanced Computer Vision course project, or is the red-blood-cell classifier intended for further development?
What is the source and licensing status of the microscopy dataset, and can a reproducible subset or download procedure be published?
Which result should be considered authoritative: the 59.52% validation result in `image_vit.ipynb` or the later majority-class result in the final notebook?
Was the Streamlit classification and image-generation diagram an intended deliverable or only an early concept?
Should the repository be retained as a coursework reference or formally archived?

evidence.summary: Supplied snapshot identifies a public repository on `main`, with no description, open issues, or open pull requests, last pushed on 2024-05-20.

The 32 tracked files comprise six notebooks, one architecture PDF, tuner JSON records, and three HDF5 checkpoints; no README, manifest, tests, CI, dataset, application entry point, license, or gitignore is present.
Executed exploratory notebooks copy TIFF files into morphology directories, count class files, inspect images, and report 64-by-64 image dimensions; they use an external-drive path.
Both notebooks contain filename-based preparation and TensorFlow directory-generator pipelines for eight morphology classes.

Implements a Keras Vision Transformer and ten-trial random search. Recorded outputs show 523 training and 126 validation images, a 59.52% best validation result, two model-loading errors, and machine-specific paths.

Implements an augmented and class-weighted Vision Transformer experiment with eighty tuning trials and a 52,797,704-parameter final model. The recorded report has 46% accuracy and predicts only the 58-sample echinocyte class in the 126-image validation set.
Ten completed tuner trial records all store a score of 0.460317462682724; trials 07 through 09 include HDF5 checkpoints totaling approximately 88 MB.
A one-page draft connects a user and Streamlit interface to uploaded-image classification, image generation, loaded models, and output results.
The four available commits span 2024-04-26 through 2024-05-20 and are generic file-upload commits; no later maintenance evidence, tags, or additional local branches are present.

confidence.rationale: All locally tracked source and experiment metadata were inspected, and they strongly support classification as a coursework prototype. Confidence is reduced because the dataset is absent, the notebooks were not reproducibly re-run, evaluation methodology is flawed, committed tuner scores conflict with a notebook result, and live GitHub release metadata was inaccessible.

limitations: The dataset and its provenance were unavailable, so preprocessing assumptions and label quality could not be verified.
Notebook execution was not reproduced because required data and a pinned environment are absent.
Binary HDF5 checkpoints were inventoried but not loaded or behaviorally evaluated.
The clone was supplied under a depth-50 history constraint, so conclusions about long-term history rely on the four commits available locally.
Live GitHub archival, release, and remote-branch state could not be independently verified because GitHub API access failed.
No credential-like filenames were found in the inspected tree; secret values were not searched for or read.
